newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent dips ahead of NYMEX, Jan support $23.30.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent dips ahead of NYMEX, Jan support $23.30.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil drifted lower around midday as the market consolidated after recent gains.

The prospect of Iraqi oil sales was also causing some concern but technical analysts saw any dips below $23.30 a barrel as a buying opportunity. An oil official in Baghdad said that it was possible Iraqi oil could hit world markets as soon as next week.
On Monday the United Nations said that an inspection of oil metering equipment by Dutch firm Saybolt was the last step before the Iraq/U.N. oil-for-food plan could start running.
Jan Brent was off 22 cents at $23.40 a barrel at 1404 GMT.

U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa on Monday did not give a start date for the plan -- which U.N. officials hope could begin next week -- but said Saybolt was to arrive in Iraq on Tuesday and it would take a couple of days to check the meter is working
"There has been some selling ahead of the Merc opening but the physical market is still well supported," said a broker.
Physical Brent nudged a couple of cents higher to 35 cents above January and dealers saw delays in loading Russian crude.
Intermonth spreads held reasonably firm with the Jan/Feb backwardation firming about eight cents to 65 cents and good demand seen.
Dec IPE gas oil futures was up $3.25 higher at $223 per tonne at the same time having opened at that level.

"Gas oil never made the arb call because heating oil was ramped up on short covering," a broker said. "People have realised that short-covering in the (New York) harbour and problems with Pemex will not affect a guy loading a barge in Antwerp."
